name: Allergies
blurb: Introducing peanut, egg and other allergens, and what prevents allergy

claims.claim: Introducing egg between 4 and 6 months reduces the risk of egg allergy
claims.testedAs: Introducing egg between 4 and 6 months reduces the risk of egg allergy

nhs.says: Introduce egg from around 6 months; delaying it past 6 to 12 months may raise the risk of egg allergy.

aap.says: Introducing egg early appears to protect against egg allergy.

claims.query: early egg introduction infant allergy prevention trial

claims.claim: Introducing peanut before 6 months of age reduces the risk of peanut allergy
claims.testedAs: Introducing peanut before 6 months of age reduces the risk of peanut allergy

nhs.says: Introduce peanut from around 6 months, when you start solids. Delaying it past 6 to 12 months may raise your baby's chance of peanut allergy.

aap.says: Babies at high risk of peanut allergy (severe eczema or egg allergy) should try peanut foods as early as 4 to 6 months, after other solids.

guidance.note: The AAP recommends peanut as early as 4 to 6 months for high-risk babies, while the NHS says around 6 months for all babies and does not recommend solids before then; both pages are current post-LEAP guidance, and neither says introducing peanut before 6 months benefits low-risk babies.

claims.query: early peanut introduction infant allergy prevention randomized

claims.claim: Introducing multiple allergenic foods early reduces overall food allergy risk
claims.testedAs: Introducing multiple allergenic foods early reduces overall food allergy risk

nhs.says: Introduce allergenic foods one at a time from around 6 months and keep them in the diet to lower allergy risk.

aap.says: Waiting past 4 to 6 months to offer allergenic foods such as egg, dairy, soy, peanut or fish does not prevent food allergy.

claims.query: early introduction multiple allergenic foods infant allergy prevention

claims.claim: Introducing peanut before 12 months reduces the risk of peanut allergy
claims.testedAs: Introducing peanut before 12 months reduces the risk of peanut allergy

nhs.says: Leaving peanut and egg out of your baby's diet past 6 to 12 months may make an allergy to them more likely.

aap.says: Holding peanut back does not protect against allergy; offer it once your baby is ready for solids, usually about 6 months.

claims.query: delayed peanut introduction infant allergy risk avoidance

claims.claim: Hydrolysed formula prevents allergic disease in high-risk infants
claims.testedAs: Hydrolysed formula prevents allergic disease in high-risk infants

aap.says: Hydrolysed formula does not prevent allergies, even in babies at high risk.

claims.query: hydrolysed formula infant allergy prevention high risk atopy

claims.claim: Eggs should be prepared well cooked to prevent illness until 12 months of age
claims.testedAs: Consumption of raw or lightly cooked egg before 12 months increases the risk of illness

nhs.says: Eggs without the British Lion mark must be cooked solid for babies; Lion-marked hens' eggs may be raw or lightly cooked.

claims.query: cooked versus raw egg infant allergenicity introduction
